chapter_title: Concerning the Ten Things that the Ambassador bega

fills.fill: The pure air was separated from the dark air, and each was set in its own region.
fills.notes: The sequence lists ten discrete cosmological operations. After Builder/ships/wheels (construction, conveyance, distribution of life), the next demanded act is a separation at the atmospheric/median level (air as the intermediate that carries influx). This matches the standard Iranian-Manichaean cosmogonic logic: a sifting of the mixed substance into purer and darker strata before the subsequent opening of the ship-doors to discharge/receive the remaining refuse (¶6–7).
Fits the oldest-layer usage: Sin here is not moral exhortation but the concretized residue/condensate separated from the rulers through the Third Ambassador’s action, then precipitating to earth.

fills.fill: from one another, and each received its measure
fills.notes: After the fall of the Sin upon earth (a precipitation of gross darkness), the next ordered operation is temporal differentiation: the separation of alternating states (night/day). The added clause ‘each received its measure’ supplies the correspondential necessity of fixed alternation/limits (measure, boundary) as part of cosmic ordering, without importing later devotional language.

assessment: Two fills (¶8, ¶10) are secure because the immediate syntax and technical cosmological usage constrain them. ¶5 and ¶9 require reconstruction at the level of cosmological logic rather than surviving wording; the proposed restorations follow the ordered sequence of (1) construction, (2) conveyance, (3) distribution, (4) separation/stratification, (5–6) opening of channels for discharge/reception, (7) precipitation of residue, (8) temporal ordering, (9) descent of malformed products, (10) cyclic transmigration in the zone. Exact original phrasing for ¶5 and ¶9 remains only moderately constrained.
